The late Pope Francis recounted three encounters with what he described as the devil and a terrifying vision of the entrance to hell in his private diaries published posthumously on Tuesday. The diaries also reveal that the pontiff experienced a two-year spiritual crisis between 2021 and 2022, during which he struggled with temptations associated with power and the exercise of authority. The revelations are contained in The Private Diary of Pope Francis, a 160-page book written by Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, one of the late pope’s closest aides and a fellow Argentine. According to CNN, which reported the revelations on Tuesday, the book contains entries from diaries Francis kept intermittently between 1992 and 2024, first as a bishop in Argentina and later as pope. The volume reveals that Francis faced “frequent demonic attacks” and detailed three encounters with the devil—two while he was archbishop of Buenos Aires and a third in 2018 after his election as pope. In an August 18, 2024 entry, Francis wrote of the devil’s “eyes of fire,” describing them as “menacing” and “seductive.” “I can’t forget his eyes the first two times — from the car when I was returning to the house, and in the choir loft during Mass. However, he always reappears in different situations,” he noted. The third encounter came shortly after a 2018 trip to Chile overshadowed by the clerical sexual abuse scandal. In a January 24, 2021 entry, Francis recalled: “On one occasion, a few days after returning to Rome, I was in a meeting. I saw him and heard his voice [his underlining], triumphant, possessing everything: ‘Now I’ve gotten everything I wanted.’ Just as I can’t forget his eyes from the previous two, in this case, I can’t forget the powerful raspiness of his voice. The Lord granted me an opportunity to leave that meeting, and he thus freed me.” Based on Catholic teaching, the devil is a fallen angel. Catholic tradition cautions that those who are serious about attaining holiness will often encounter strong spiritual opposition. The diaries also describe a vision of “the entrance to hell” in 2018, which Francis characterized as a form of “pagan seduction in full force.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The book reveals that Francis experienced a spiritual crisis in 2021 and 2022, which Fernández linked to temptations associated with power, excessive activity and feelings of self-sufficiency. The late pontiff reportedly described the crisis as involving “governance issues, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation.” To overcome the temptation, Francis sought to practise greater humility and patience, including by retaining some officials in the Church’s central administration despite criticism of their conduct. Fernández recalled an occasion when a bishop asked Francis why he had not dismissed an official in the Roman Curia who had publicly criticised him and pursued what the bishop considered a different agenda. “After an interminable silence, he responded by explaining that he felt a strong sensation in his heart that God did not want him to become a puppeteer who uses and manipulates people according to his own convenience. He explained that, for this reason, he preferred to let that person remain in his position,” Fernández wrote. In an entry dated December 30, 2022, Francis said he had resisted the temptation to treat “others like puppets”. I can’t forget the day I saw it,” he wrote. Fernández explained that the crisis was connected to Francis’ struggle with the temptation to discover what it meant to exercise personal power. He added that the pope considered feeling “above the world” through power to be “the path of the worst spiritual worldliness imaginable”. The diaries also contain Francis’ reflections on the clerical sexual abuse scandal in Chile in 2018, when he faced criticism for his handling of allegations against a bishop accused of witnessing and covering up abuse. The pope later apologised for his handling of the case and summoned Chilean bishops to Rome, where they collectively offered their resignations. “Devastated because of the situation in Chile and the dialogue with the journalists on the airplane. I fell off the cot then,” Francis wrote. The book explains that the expression “fell off the cot” means suddenly waking up to something. The diaries also reveal Francis’ assessment of Cardinal Robert Prevost, who succeeded him as Pope Leo XIV. According to Fernández, Francis described Prevost as “a great pastor, a generous missionary, and an irreproachable man”. He also praised other cardinals who had criticised him, describing Cardinal Robert Sarah as having “a refined spiritual sensitivity” and saying of Cardinal Gerhard Muller that he “seems aggressive but he’s a good man”. The entries further show Francis’ frequent exhaustion and dedication to his ministry. In 2019, he described himself as “feeling exhausted, almost without spiritual support and without a point of reference”. Francis, who became the first Latin American pope when he was elected on March 13, 2013, died on April 21, 2025, aged 88, after being hospitalised with double pneumonia. His funeral was held on April 26, 2025, at St Peter’s Square in the Vatican. Fernández said the diaries were intended to reveal the heart of Jorge Mario Bergoglio, the late pope’s birth name. “His total dedication, coupled with frequently feeling completely exhausted, speaks of heroism in pastoral charity,” he said. The diaries are being published by the Vatican Publishing House, while Image Books, an imprint of Penguin Random House Christian Publishing Group, is releasing the English-language edition in the United States and Canada.
